summary: Timer start/capture: records a fresh high-resolution timestamp into the timer's previous-query fields (offset 0x30 low part, offset 0x34 high part) for later delta computation. Only writes when the timer is initialized (offset 0x0 non-zero) and both timestamp fields are currently zero, so it behaves as a one-shot start guard. Source of the timestamp is selected by a mode flag at offset 0x48: bit 0 set uses QueryPerformanceCounter, otherwise RDTSC via RDTSCTimestampRead.

operations.description: Read timer state at offset 0x0; if zero (timer not initialized) skip timestamp capture and return the existing value.
If the previous-query high part at offset 0x34 is already non-zero, skip and return the existing value.
If the previous-query low part at offset 0x30 is already non-zero, skip and return the existing value.
Inspect the mode flags at offset 0x48; bit 0 set selects the QueryPerformanceCounter path, otherwise the RDTSC path.
QueryPerformanceCounter fills a 64-bit performance counter into a local LARGE_INTEGER.
Store the captured counter: high part to offset 0x34, low part to offset 0x30.
RDTSC path: call RDTSCTimestampRead with pointers to offsets 0x34 and 0x30 as the timestamp output targets.
Return the timer state value; a zero result means the capture was skipped.
